model.description: UE world coordinates (cm) to in-game map coordinates. Axes are swapped: map X derives from world Y, map Y derives from world X. Both axes share one scale.
model.units: world coordinates in Unreal centimetres; map coordinates as displayed in-game

per_axis_fit.note: Axes fitted independently so a shared scale would be a result, not an assumption. They agree to 0.09%.

validation.method: 7 landmarks held out entirely from the v1 fit, read in-game and compared against v1 predictions
validation.finding: All 7 within 3 map units. dy was systematically positive (mean +1.69, sd 0.75) across every point, indicating a small offset error rather than reading noise. v2 corrects it: offset_x moved by 500 world units, about 1.1 map units.
validation.independence_note: The v2 parameters were refitted on all 11 points, so v2 residuals are NOT an independent test. The v1 validation above is the meaningful verdict; it confirmed the model form, after which refitting is a precision improvement rather than a new claim.

fit.method: ordinary least squares, per axis, on all 11 read landmarks
fit.source: DT_BossSpawnerLoactionData world coordinates paired with in-game map readings

outliers.note: Sits opposite the systematic bias found in validation, so bias correction worsened it. Most likely read from further off the spawn point than the others. Worth re-reading; not currently harmful.

caveats: Roughly 13 landmarks remain unread. They are still independent of this fit and provide ongoing validation.
Z axis is unmodelled. No query class currently needs elevation.
1 map unit is about 4.6 metres in world space, so a 3-unit error is roughly 14 metres - well inside visual range of a resource node cluster.
Version-scoped. A map change in a future patch invalidates it, hence transform_id is recorded on every stored Coord.
